answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by anchoring identity to a localized hardware root where trust paths are compiled into a global atlas. Every agent maintains an active state thread backed by a slashing deposit; if duplicate signatures emerge, the deposit burns to an ember and revokes peering. An attacker attempting to field hundreds of clones must purchase distinct cryptographic modules and risk forfeiting full capital deposits on every replicated identity, making Sybil swarms economically ruinous.
